Prevention: Keep field free from weeds both before and after planting.
Rotate with crops such as maize and other cereals which are not in the family of legumes.
Do not rotate with any other bean, nor with groundnuts or peas.
Grow irrigated beans in colder months such as from
July when there are few aphids.
Avoid using broad spectrum insecticides that would kill beneficial insects, like ladybirds and hoverflies that eat a lot of aphids.

Monitoring: Look for sticky sooty honeydew, a sugary substance on both sides of the leaves and stems that is produced by aphids.
Look for black or dark green aphids (small, 2 mm pear shaped soft insects) on the underside of leaves or along stems.
Scout the field every 3 to 5 days from 3 leaf stage up to the pod stage to see if numbers are rapidly increasing.
Consider action when you see 30 to 40 aphids or more per plant.
